brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.evidence: Three cells in a row at q=-1,0,1 on level 0: piece:-1,0,0 (half-s base), piece:0,0,0 (full base), piece:1,0,0 (half-n base). Caps and joint bolts closed the open faces; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut (north half, cell -1,0) and drawer:0#1,0#cut (south half, cell 1,0). Each sits on the cut face of its half base.

setDrawerOpen applied to the drawer at cell 1,0 (open=true). The other drawer is closed. Visual confirmation from the look tool was limited (no parts reported in view), so the open state is recorded by the op result rather than a rendered view.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell cabinet: a full base in the middle with a south-half base on the west and a north-half base on the east, each half carrying one classic drawer (the split-cell rule requires a half base paired with a drawer on the other half). The east drawer is pulled open; the west one is closed. Open faces are capped and joints locked; check_build is clean with meshClash clear.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
